function: Channel prediction: predicts future channels at arbitrary time slots from estimates at a Chebyshev-based non-uniform pilot pattern, in high-mobility MIMO (pp. 4-9).
system: BS with 32 dual-polarized UPA antennas (4x4 panels) serving one single-antenna UE; 3.5 GHz; urban macro-cell; no RIS (pp. 3, 11).
method: Encoder-decoder transformer with continuous-time attention (neural ODE values, interpolated queries and keys), high-frequency temporal encoding and element-wise prediction; supervised NMSE training, 300 epochs (pp. 7-11).
data_channel: 3GPP TR 38.901 urban macro-cell data set (3.5 GHz, 12 paths; 12,800 train, 2,560 test samples); DeepMIMO Outdoor 1 ray-tracing data set also evaluated (pp. 10-11, 15).
test_conditions: Train/test split of one 3GPP UMa data set (12,800/2,560 samples), default 60 km/h, SNR 10 dB; velocity 20-80 km/h and SNR sweeps; separate DeepMIMO data set (pp. 10-15).
baselines: Learned: GRU, vanilla transformer, neural ODE, latent ODE (ODE-Former in complexity only); non-learned: none; uniform and random pilot patterns compared as pilot designs (pp. 13-15).
metrics: NMSE (dB) versus prediction time slot, UE velocity, pilot pattern and SNR; pilot overhead; model parameters and MFLOPs (pp. 10-15).
complexity: Proposed: 176.13 M parameters and 395.59 MFLOPs (Table X); continuous-time attention O(L^2 dE) versus O(L^2 d) standard attention (pp. 8, 15).
openness: Code released at https://github.com/sangyl23/Continuous-Time-Transformer (p. 11, ref. [35] on p. 16); DeepMIMO public data set also used (p. 15).
q1_support: p. 10: "The channel model of 3GPP TR 38.901 for urban macro-cell scenarios is adopted to generate the data set in our simulations [36]"; p. 15: "DeepMIMO [64] based on Wireless InSite is used to generate ray-tracing channels".
q2_support: p. 14, Fig. 7: "NMSE performance with varying UE velocities v under different pilot patterns and deep learning models"; the paper never states that a model trained in one velocity, scenario or data set is tested in another (default v = 60 km/h, p. 10; DeepMIMO is a separate data set, p. 15).
q3_support: p. 13: "Fig. 6 compares the NMSE performance of different pilot patterns and deep learning models"; the compared predictors are GRU, vanilla transformer, neural ODE and latent ODE, all learned, and no AR, Kalman, Prony or outdated-channel baseline appears in Section V.
q4_support: p. 15: "Table X compares the model parameters and computational complexity of different deep learning models" (176.13 M parameters, 395.59 MFLOPs for the proposed model); p. 8, Remark 5 gives the order O(L^2 dE).
q5_support: p. 11: "The source codes of our simulations have been released at [35]"; p. 16, ref. [35]: "https://github.com/sangyl23/Continuous-Time-Transformer".
notes: Area 2 (channel prediction). The Chebyshev non-uniform pilot pattern is a closed-form design, not learned; the learned element is the continuous-time transformer. q3=0 because no non-learned channel predictor is compared (uniform and random pilot patterns are pilot designs fed to the same learned models); reviewer may confirm. The PDF looks like the IEEE Xplore published version (journal pages 12497-12512), although the list gives preprint. Table contents were read from page images.
